sourcing_note: Follow-up to newly-sourced-batch-11.json (ARDX): re-running the full select_frozen_cohort(seed=100100) dry-run after committing ARDX showed the selected-cohort negative count unchanged at 39/40, not 40 as an isolated single-candidate prediction had suggested. Root-caused via a same-year before/after selected-set diff: ARDX landed in REGULATORY/2021, the same (stratum, year) bucket as an already-selected negative candidate (REG-2021-OMER-NARSOPLIMAB-CRL) - inserting ARDX into that year's shuffle cascaded the round-robin cursor and displaced OMER from the selected set, a like-for-like negative-for-negative swap with zero net gain. This is the non-linear cascading effect in a sharper form: a same-year addition can cannibalize an existing selection instead of adding to it. Corrected methodology: re-ran the greedy single-slot search as a full end-to-end selected-set delta (add one hypothetical candidate per (stratum, year), re-run the complete real selection, and diff the resulting negative count against the current real baseline - not an isolated marginal-effect estimate) across every populated year in every stratum. REGULATORY/2020 was the strongest result (+2 net, not just +1), because that year currently has no pre-existing negative candidate in the selected set to be cannibalized. Sourced one real FDA Complete Response Letter for that exact slot: Liquidia's November 2020 CRL for LIQ861 (treprostinil inhalation powder, later approved and branded Yutrepia). CORRECTION (see newly-sourced-batch-13.json for the full account): the full dry-run simulation run against the real post-addition pool showed the selected-cohort negative count reached exactly 40/40, not the predicted 41 - LQDA itself was not selected (REGULATORY/2020 already had 30 higher-priority candidates ahead of it in that year's post-shuffle order), but its insertion still shifted the shared-RNG state consumed by the subsequent REGULATORY/2021 shuffle, which pulled the previously-unselected REG-2021-ARDX-TENAPANOR-CRL into the selected set in place of a non-negative candidate (REG-2021-APLS-EMPAVELI). Net effect: +1 negative, delivered indirectly via a two-hop cascade rather than the predicted direct addition, landing exactly at the 40/40 requirement with zero margin. This satisfies the frozen requirement but not this workstream's preference for real buffer over an exact match, so sourcing continued in batch-13 (Kura Oncology), which was confirmed to bring the total to 41/40.

events.company: Liquidia Technologies, Inc. (subsidiary of Liquidia Corporation)
events.notes: FDA CRL for LIQ861 (NDA seeking approval for PAH) stated the FDA is 'unable to approve the NDA at this time,' citing CMC data on the drug product and device biocompatibility, plus a reconfirmed need for on-site pre-approval facility inspections (COVID-19 travel restrictions had prevented them during the initial review cycle). The CRL did not cite need for additional clinical, toxicology, or clinical pharmacology studies - a CMC/facilities-focused rejection, comparable in kind to the already-pooled REG-2024-RCKT-KRESLADI-CRL, but still an unambiguous NDA rejection and approval delay (issuer's own release: 'FDA...has issued a complete response letter'). LIQ861 was eventually approved as Yutrepia in 2025 after further CRLs and litigation, none of which is inspected or referenced here - only the November 2020 CRL's own first-public disclosure is used.
